name: Lucas Lepri Half Guard Passing System
description: Study gi half-guard passing with a focused Lucas Lepri course match, practical partner drills, clear decisions, and ways to review your progress.
summary: The Lucas Lepri Half Guard Passing System organizes top-half-guard control around lapel grips, responses to the bottom player coming up, and adjustments against deep-half and knee-shield variations.
overview:
Top half guard is a family of different exchanges. The bottom player may be flattened, building to a single leg, or moving under the hips into deep half. Classifying that change before selecting a pass gives a training partner a clear defensive task and gives you a useful way to review the result.

Precise Half Guard Passing by Lucas Lepri is the matched instructional. The syllabus covers lapel-assisted knee cuts, coyote and single-leg reactions, deep-half control, and a backstep against Z-guard. The drills, sequence, and assessment criteria below are an original BJJGraph study plan; use them to organize practice alongside the course and feedback from a coach.
key_principles: Identify the half-guard variation before selecting the pass.
Check what a lapel grip controls rather than merely holding it.
Respond when the defender starts coming up, not only after standing.
Re-establish base as the defender moves under the hips.
Separate passing practice from later submission study.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Every variation receives the same pressure response.
common_obstacles.solution: Name whether the defender is shielding, coming up, or entering deep half before acting.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A lapel grip occupies the hand without limiting movement.
common_obstacles.solution: Pause and ask a coach to check its purpose and positioning.

common_obstacles.obstacle: The defender reaches the knees before you notice the change.
common_obstacles.solution: Use an early-reaction drill that ends as soon as the coming-up attempt is established.

common_obstacles.obstacle: A base switch frees the trapped leg but concedes a reversal.
common_obstacles.solution: Rehearse the base adjustment with limited resistance before reconnecting the pass.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: Choose a reviewed lapel connection in top half guard and test whether the defender can turn or establish an underhook before adding the pass. Then connect it to coming-up reaction. Compare the first lost control point after each round. Keep the first repetitions cooperative and agree on resistance, space, and reset conditions. Once the starting task is clear, add one defensive option at a time and compare the result with the intended control objective.

flashcards.question: Why should top half guard be divided into different scenarios?
flashcards.answer: A knee shield, a coming-up attempt, and deep half create different control problems and may require different passing responses.

flashcards.question: What should a lapel-control drill measure?
flashcards.answer: Measure which movement the grip restricts and whether the defender can turn or establish the next useful connection.

flashcards.question: When does a coming-up reaction need attention?
flashcards.answer: Recognize it as the defender starts building toward the knees or a single leg, before treating the exchange as a routine pass.

flashcards.question: What is the first focus when the opponent moves into deep half?
flashcards.answer: Re-establish a usable base and identify the hip control before adding a leg-clearing action.

flashcards.question: Why practice a backstep cooperatively before increasing resistance?
flashcards.answer: The base changes during the movement, so a slow rehearsal lets both partners identify when control is lost.

flashcards.question: How does this study plan use the course's submission material?
flashcards.answer: It begins with control and passing; submission sections can be studied later without making them prerequisites for the first positional drills.
